system.description:
Origins

The Syrne created the Eldarin as soldiers for their ancient war. When their makers perished, the Eldarin were left scattered across the crystal spheres with no homeland. They built immense worldships holding whole ecosystems and now wander the Astral Sea, occasionally, after years of research, bringing a Portal Relay back online, and keeping the relays working with the scraps of knowledge that survive.

An Eldarin's home is a ship rather than a town, and those in good standing take its name as their surname. Life inside fragile artificial habitats makes them careful and conservative, unwilling to upset any balance. Youths must undertake a pilgrimage to show they are self-reliant: those who return with something of value become adults, and the rest die — a deliberate form of population control.

Appearance

They are about human height or a little taller but fragile and poor at taking punishment. Men and women alike are slender and beautiful, with sharp features, long pointed ears and high cheekbones. Most are physically weak, partly from shipboard life and partly because their society honours artists and poets while machines do the manual work.

Having rarely seen natural sunlight, they are almost always pale. Off-ship they wear sealed environment suits, often with opaque masks, so outsiders come to know the suit rather than the person — showing one's bare face is a sign of great trust. They mature like humans, then age extremely slowly and stay healthy until the end of lives that often span centuries.

In Play

Everything in Eldarin life is geared to survival and to preserving what they have; resources are scarce and seldom traded. Most have strong psychic gifts, and many become sorcerers or at least dabble in magic. What they guard most carefully is the soul: their bond with the Warp makes their souls tempting prey for daemons, so it is customary to wear a soulstone that captures the soul at death instead of letting it drift into the Warp. Few believe in an afterlife, though most honour some deity for protection or power.

Eldarin distrust any environment beyond their ships. Sterile upbringings leave many with weak immune systems, and anything dirty or involving manual labour is simply not done.

Relations

Eldarin and Dark Eldarin glare at each other across any room, each waiting for an excuse to kill the other. Elves, in Eldarin eyes, are cousins who have regressed into primitive barbarism and deserve pity.

Example heroes (p. 35): Talieer, Mecheldr, Giorna.

power.name: Warp Step
power.description:
As a half action, teleport a distance of up to double your Speed to a spot you can see.

Uses per scene: 1 at Level 1, 2 from Level 3, 3 from Level 5.
